content.text:
The child who only says "I'm bored" even in the forest

You've finally taken a trip out into nature, but your child just looks for their smartphone or grumbles, "I'm bored, when are we leaving?" It's a little disappointing to see them walk right past a beautiful forest.

A child finds nature dull because they haven't yet felt it with their five senses. With just a small spark to open their eyes and ears, the forest becomes the most wonderful playground in the world.

Curious about the plot of this nature observation storybook? We take a look at the lessons of the nature observation storybook through pictures. Meet the key scenes of the nature observation storybook's story, too. Read the nature observation storybook together with your child and talk about it. We've gathered all kinds of stories about "45. Thank You, Nature!"—including environment storybooks, autumn forest storybooks, and nature experience storybooks.

content.alt: 45. Thank You, Nature! - Why sensitivity to nature matters
content.text:
Why sensitivity to nature matters

Feeling nature with all five senses grows both a child's curiosity and their emotions. A child who knows the sound of fallen leaves, the smell of earth, and the touch of an acorn sees the world more richly.

And a child who feels grateful to nature comes to want to cherish and protect it. Small acts like picking up litter and keeping things clean grow from this sensitivity, planted in early childhood.
content.caption: A child who feels it with all five senses comes to cherish and protect nature.

content.alt: 45. Thank You, Nature! - Hori's story of learning to be thankful for the forest
content.text:
Hori's story of learning to be thankful for the forest

In Thank You, Nature!, Hori is indifferent to the autumn forest. Then Mom covers his eyes and asks, "What sounds can you hear?" As the rustle of leaves, the whoosh of wind, and the chirp of birds reach him, Hori is amazed.

Having felt the forest with his whole body, Hori hugs a tree and says, "The forest was giving me so much!" On the way out, he even picks up the litter that's fallen. "Leave it as clean as we found it!" Along with Hori, a child learns the heart that leads from gratitude to action.
content.caption: Once he knew all the forest gives, his heart filled with gratitude.

content.alt: 45. Thank You, Nature! - Nature games to play together on your outings
content.text:
Nature games to play together on your outings

When you go to a forest or park, try the "close your eyes and listen" game. Listening closely to the sounds of fallen leaves, wind, and birds lets your child meet nature with all five senses. Picking up acorns and collecting pretty leaves are great games too.

On your way back, tidy up the spot where you played together and practice "leave it as clean as you found it." A small habit of saying "Thank you, tree" plants in your child's heart a sensitivity that cherishes nature.

content.text:
Frequently Asked Questions

Q. How should I observe nature with my child?

A. As you take a walk, look closely at flowers, trees, and bugs together, and say "Thank you, nature." The experience of carefully noticing small things grows your child's curiosity and sensitivity.

Q. How does a nature observation storybook help?

A. Watching the character cherish and pay attention to nature, a child learns to value living things and the environment. A nature observation storybook nurtures a warm eye toward the world.

Q. How do I draw in a child who isn't interested in nature?

A. Rather than giving the answers, wonder together about what you can see and explore joyfully. Sharing the joy of discovery makes a child want to learn more about nature on their own.
